Two-part models

Source: R/twopart.R
suest_twopart.Rd

suest_twopart() combines the two parts of a two-part model (Stata's twopm): a binary model for whether the outcome is positive, fit to everyone, and a model for the outcome among those with a positive outcome. Predictions, slopes, and comparisons from marginaleffects are then on the overall expected outcome, Pr(y > 0) * E(y | y > 0), with standard errors from the joint covariance matrix of the two parts.

Usage

suest_twopart(first, second, model_names = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'suest_twopart'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

first

Binary logit, probit, or complementary log-log model for whether the outcome is positive.

second

Model for the outcome among the observations with a positive outcome: a linear model or a GLM, for example a Gamma model or a Poisson pseudo-likelihood model (quasipoisson()) with a log link.

model_names

Names of the two parts. By default, the object names supplied in the call.

...

Passed to suest(), for example cluster, weight_type, or survey_design with observation_id.

x

A "suest_twopart" object.

Value

An object of class c("suest_twopart", "suest_model").

Details

Fit the second part to every observation in the first part's sample that has a positive outcome, for example with subset = y > 0. Without newdata, results are averaged over the first part's estimation sample. type = "response" (the default) gives the overall expected outcome, type = "prob" the probability of a positive outcome (the first part), and type = "conditional" the expected outcome among those with a positive outcome (the second part).

Examples

dat <- mtcars
dat$y <- ifelse(dat$am == 1, dat$mpg, 0)
any <- glm(I(y > 0) ~ wt, family = binomial(), data = dat)
amount <- glm(y ~ wt, family = Gamma(link = "log"), data = dat, subset = y > 0)
fit <- suest_twopart(any, amount)
marginaleffects::avg_slopes(fit, variables = "wt")
#> 
#>  Estimate Std. Error     z Pr(>|z|)    S 2.5 % 97.5 %
#>     -10.7      0.953 -11.2   <0.001 94.5 -12.5  -8.82
#> 
#> Term: wt
#> Type: response
#> Comparison: dY/dX
#>
